summary: This study used custom-made optical coherence tomography to obtain 2-μm thin-slice en face images of the lamina cribrosa (LC) in 13 eyes from 10 primary open angle glaucoma (POAG) patients and 10 eyes from 7 normal controls. The study measured elongation indices (EIs) of lamina pores at different depth levels, finding that EIs were greater at the anterior surface and 40-μm depth level in POAG eyes compared to normal eyes. The results suggest that nerve fiber bundles passing through the LC were under greater stress in the anterior layers of the LC in POAG eyes.
